mbm-0418.clue: I wear the little green flag.
mbm-0418.quote: We forgot our beach volleyball flags, so I tied my green bandanna to the corner rope. When I wore it home afterward there was one perfect knot full of sand. I keep that knot for close games.

mbm-0419.clue: I ask for a coin with a scratch.
mbm-0419.quote: The audience can recognize their own coin by the scratch when it turns up in my little glass jar. Last Saturday the owner recognized a second scratch too. It was his sister’s coin, borrowed years ago.

mbm-0420.clue: I still use the glass with a chip in the foot.
mbm-0420.quote: I made a silk flower bloom beneath an upside-down glass. A chip in its base caught the sun and sent a little flash across the petals. I couldn’t plan such good lighting if I tried.

mbm-0421.clue: I know when the disc wants to come home.
mbm-0421.quote: I threw it into a stiff wind and watched it float back over my shoulder. My younger cousin caught it without leaving his picnic blanket. He’s been asking me for room service ever since.

mbm-0422.clue: I keep my feet in the picture.
mbm-0422.quote: I photographed my climbing shoes at the top of our practice wall because I thought nobody would believe I’d reached it. My friend’s smiling face is reflected in the little metal anchor beside my toes.

mbm-0423.clue: My pace has a four-legged coach.
mbm-0423.quote: A little terrier trots along the inside of a garden fence on my morning run. When I slow down, he doubles back. The day I wore new shoes he inspected both of them through the gate.

mbm-0424.clue: I dance where I can see the paint.
mbm-0424.quote: At our club the owner painted yellow stars around one column. I met my best dance partner beside the crooked one. We return to that star when the room fills up and the music starts.

mbm-0425.clue: I leave one bridge for my brother.
mbm-0425.quote: My brother is much better at the building game. When I spot a river I pause and hand him the controller. The most ridiculous bridge we ever made has steps, a rooftop garden and exactly one sheep.

mbm-0426.clue: I kept the cream off the camera.
mbm-0426.quote: I ate my first contest cream puff over a paper plate, and the filling shot straight at my friend’s lens. The lens cap was still on. He says it remains the best picture he almost took.

mbm-0427.clue: I know which token belongs on the stove.
mbm-0427.quote: We lost the little cooking pot in our kitchen board game and substituted a thimble. I turn it upside down and balance one grain of rice on top. Guests are delighted when I serve the winning player supper.

mbm-0428.clue: I can see rain before I feel it.
mbm-0428.quote: From my canoe I watch the round marks race across a smooth pond before the first drop reaches my sleeve. I lift one corner of the bright yellow hood my sister lent me. I always wait for one more ring.

mbm-0429.clue: I quilt in a little breeze.
mbm-0429.quote: My worktable stands beside a window. The yellow patch in my latest quilt kept lifting every time I reached for a needle. I stitched it into a kite and left its tail a little loose.

mbm-0430.clue: I pack the summit in my sandwich box.
mbm-0430.quote: I never take stones from the peak. I put a scrap of tracing paper over the nicest one and rub it with a pencil. On rainy evenings the sandwich box opens onto a whole mountain range.

mbm-0431.clue: I paint my thumbnail before a match.
mbm-0431.quote: A tiny blue dot reminds me which side of the beach court the wind came from when we arrived. My niece changes the color if the breeze turns at lunchtime. She takes the job very seriously.

mbm-0432.clue: I keep one scarf in the bread tin.
mbm-0432.quote: The lightest juggling scarf floated onto a bakery awning during a street show. The baker handed it back in a paper bread bag. Now it smells faintly of cinnamon every time it sails past my face.

mbm-0433.clue: I watch the shadow of the umbrella spokes.
mbm-0433.quote: When the spokes' shadows reach the blue edge of my towel I turn my chair and open the cold grapes. My friend says I’ve invented a lunch clock that only works on excellent days.

mbm-0434.clue: I always save a place for the hat.
mbm-0434.quote: The river lifted my friend's hat clean off and set it on the bow of our raft. We paddled a whole quiet stretch with the hat riding proudly up front, like a very small captain.

mbm-0435.clue: I keep the shells from the sidelines.
mbm-0435.quote: When we play beach volleyball my little sister chooses four shells for corner markers. After dark I put them in a jar. Shake it and I can hear a whole summer of disputed points.

mbm-0436.clue: I stitched four sleeves into the sky.
mbm-0436.quote: For Dad’s retirement quilt I used the blue cuffs of his four favorite shirts. The darker bits became clouds. He recognized each shirt before he noticed I’d given him a whole evening sky.

mbm-0437.clue: I find the smallest one first.
mbm-0437.quote: At the dumpling contest I chose the smallest dumpling on the plate and drew a face on its paper wrapper afterward. The drawing became my very unofficial mascot. I didn’t win, but the mascot drew a crowd.

mbm-0438.clue: I owe my best shot to a red umbrella.
mbm-0438.quote: I was struggling to pick a target on a long fairway when my sister popped open her umbrella beside the green. I aimed for the red shape and landed just short. She still takes half the credit.

mbm-0439.clue: My movie-night pass comes with a tassel.
mbm-0439.quote: I knotted a little tassel onto our old remote so it stops disappearing into the sofa. Now we pass it like a royal baton at pajama movie night. The person holding it gets the first choice of film.

mbm-0440.clue: I dried the river on the railing.
mbm-0440.quote: After we carried the raft ashore we spread our soaked bandannas along a rail. Each had a different stripe of muddy water at the bottom. My friend photographed the row like a very honest crew portrait.

mbm-0441.clue: I sign my turns in the snow.
mbm-0441.quote: My ski instructor asked me to make two smooth linked turns. When I looked back I’d signed the last letter of my name. I’ll need a lot more practice for the first four.

mbm-0442.clue: I put a little mirror beside the camera.
mbm-0442.quote: At a party I used a pocket mirror to bounce sunlight onto my friend’s dark glasses. In the print you can see a tiny gold window reflected in each lens. That’s the whole trick I was after.
